title: Ordinary sheaf tensor through a ringed-site equivalence
statement: Let C and D be categories essentially small relative to a universe w, J and K Grothendieck topologies on them [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and e : C ≌ D an equivalence whose functor and inverse are continuous for J and K. Let R be a sheaf of commutative rings on (D,K), S one on (C,J), and c : S ≅ e^s R a coefficient isomorphism. Write F : Mod(R) → Mod(S) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for precomposition along e.functor followed by restriction of scalars along c. With ordinary sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and coefficients and modules in universe w, there is a natural isomorphism of binary functors tensor_R ⋙ F ≅ (F × F) ⋙ tensor_S. No complexes, flatness, reduction, completion, or choice of comparison as data is asserted.

source.place: section-tensor-product (03EK), lemma-tensor-product-pullback (03EL), and lemma-sheafification-tensor; ringed-site equivalence specialization of the intrinsic-to-the-topos tensor argument.

proof.text: The inverse of e is continuous, hence CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous makes it cover preserving. Apply Adjunction.isCocontinuous_iff_coverPreserving to e.toAdjunction to obtain cocontinuity of e.functor. This uses only the given continuity hypothesis and the site equivalence adjunction.

Apply sheafCompose with the forgetful functor from commutative rings to rings to the coefficient isomorphism c. The resulting isomorphism has exactly the coefficient type required by ringed_cocontinuous_monoidal. Apply that theorem to e.functor, S and R, using the given essential-smallness and continuity hypotheses and the cocontinuity proved in Step 1. Its monoidal categories are the existing localization tensor categories; their monoidality witnesses agree with isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients by proof irrelevance.

Locally install the resulting strong monoidal structure on the exact specified pushforward functor F. Functor.Monoidal.muNatIso (Lean identifier μNatIso) is a natural isomorphism F.prod F followed by tensor to tensor followed by F. Take its inverse and introduce Nonempty, obtaining the required orientation without selecting any tensor comparison as public data.

proof_origin.place: section-tensor-product, lemma-sheafification-tensor and lemma-tensor-product-pullback. Reuse the established cocontinuous ringed-module restriction theorem, with cocontinuity from the equivalence adjunction and continuity of its inverse; finish with the inverse monoidal tensorator.

theorem pushforward_equivalence_tensor_iso
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] [EssentiallySmall.{w} D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (e : C ≌ D) [e.functor.IsContinuous J K] [e.inverse.IsContinuous K J]
    (R : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{w}) (S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (c : S ≅ (e.functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{w} J K).obj R) :
    letI := isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients R
    letI := isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients S
    letI := monoidalCategory R
    letI := monoidalCategory S
    let F := pushforward.{w} (F := e.functor) (J := J) (K := K)
      (R := (sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).obj R)
      (S := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).obj S)
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).map c.hom)
    Nonempty (tensor _ ⋙ F ≅ F.prod F ⋙ tensor _)
